summary:
Earth System Trend Detective is an environmental data analysis platform designed to identify and understand changes in Earth's interconnected environmental systems. The project uses NASA POWER data covering 2001–2025, including temperature, precipitation, relative humidity and other atmospheric variables.

The system processes and segregates environmental datasets using Python, prepares structured datasets for WEKA, and applies machine-learning techniques to discover environmental patterns and clusters. Statistical methods, including Linear Regression, the Mann-Kendall test and Sen's Slope, are used to investigate the direction, magnitude and significance of long-term environmental trends.

An interactive dashboard presents trend statistics, visualizations and scientific findings in an understandable format. The project aims to make Earth science data analysis more accessible and support better understanding of environmental changes through data-driven investigation.
details:
Project Overview

Earth System Trend Detective is a data-driven environmental monitoring and trend analysis platform developed to investigate long-term changes in Earth's environmental systems using NASA Earth science data.

How It Works

The project follows an integrated data analysis workflow:

  1. NASA Data Collection: Environmental datasets are obtained from NASA POWER, covering the period 2001–2025 for the selected study location.
  2. Data Segregation: Python is used to clean, organize, filter and separate environmental variables such as temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, specific humidity and wind parameters.
  3. Machine Learning with WEKA: Structured datasets are prepared in CSV and ARFF formats for exploratory machine-learning analysis, including SimpleKMeans clustering and environmental pattern discovery.
  4. Statistical Trend Detection: Linear Regression, Mann-Kendall testing and Sen's Slope are used to identify increasing or decreasing trends, estimate their magnitude and evaluate statistical significance.
  5. Visualization: An interactive dashboard presents environmental trend results, graphs and statistical findings.

Technologies Used

  • NASA POWER – Earth science data source.
  • Python – Data processing and segregation.
  • Pandas and NumPy – Data handling and numerical processing.
  • SciPy – Statistical analysis.
  • WEKA – Machine learning and clustering.
  • HTML and CSS – Dashboard interface.
  • CSV and ARFF – Scientific dataset formats.

Innovation and Creativity

The project's key innovation is integrating NASA environmental datasets, automated data preparation, machine-learning-based pattern discovery and statistical trend analysis into one workflow. Instead of simply displaying environmental measurements, the platform investigates whether variables are changing, identifies the direction and magnitude of trends, and evaluates their statistical significance.

Intended Impact

The project aims to make Earth science data more accessible to students, researchers and environmental enthusiasts. Its analytical framework can be extended to multiple geographical regions and additional NASA Earth observation datasets to support regional environmental comparisons and climate research.

Limitations and Future Development

The current prototype uses a single geographical location. Future development will include multi-region analysis, additional NASA Earth observation datasets, automated data updates, spatial trend mapping and expanded environmental comparisons.
